inline.s: A Personal Account of a Buddha-Reciter
[Dual cultivation of nature and life] Cultivation of nature: liberation of one's own nature (escaping the six realms of samsara); cultivation of life: health and longevity.

I have been sickly since childhood, frail in body, and constantly tormented by health problems. More than ten years ago, a thought kept circling in my mind: in this life, even if I can do nothing else, at least I can cease evil and do good, and be a good person — surely I can manage that! Looking back now, this was the turning point of my fate.

Knock, and the door will open. Because of this aspiration, circumstances followed in succession, enabling me to study Liao Fan's Four Lessons and to uphold the Sutra of the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and to recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. After unremitting effort, my health gradually improved over several years. I then began, following

I have had a realization: before, I could never encounter many good opportunities, and even when I did, I would not believe or accept them, but instead embrace bad ones. After ceasing evil, doing good, and practicing Buddha-recitation, the situation reversed; I encountered many good opportunities and could seize them in time.
Along with breathing Buddha-recitation, I also practiced

. Having opened the Conception and Governing vessels, I practiced every day, and diligent Buddha-recitation continually dissolved my karma, so my body grew better and better. Yet practice and Buddha-recitation are after all two separate things, and I often wondered: could they be combined, to achieve the dual cultivation of nature and life? Fortunately, not long ago I read
and suddenly had an insight: if I do the microcosmic orbit practice while practicing breathing Buddha-recitation, combining the two, is that not the dual cultivation of nature and life?

In this way, not only during dedicated recitation but at ordinary times as well, whenever I had the chance I would practice breathing Buddha-recitation anytime and anywhere, and at the same time do the microcosmic orbit practice: inhaling while reciting 'A-mi,' exhaling while reciting 'Tuo-fo,' with the true qi circulating through the orbit accordingly. While doing walking meditation or simply walking, I would recite the four-syllable Buddha-name, one syllable per step, inhaling over four steps and exhaling over four steps, with the true qi circulating through the orbit accordingly. Thus Buddha-recitation became part of life, and practice became part of life.
Now, full of confidence, I have embarked on a new journey: while I live in this world, health and longevity; and once my life ends, certain rebirth in the Land of Bliss.
